title: Senate Appropriators Cut $20B From US Navy Shipbuilding, US Tests Unarmed ICBM Ahead of Shenzhen Summit, and Hegseth Unveils Venezuela Military Pact
subhead: US Senate appropriators slash nearly $20 billion from Navy shipbuilding as the Pentagon tests a Minuteman-class ICBM before Donald Trump's arrival in China, Pete Hegseth signs a new military deal in Venezuela, and Ukraine hits the Kerch Bridge for a third time in three days.

sections.heading: Senate Appropriators Slash $20B From Navy Shipbuilding Request
sections.body:
Senate appropriators cut nearly $20 billion from the US Navy's shipbuilding request in their draft Fiscal Year 2027 defense spending bill, allotting $41.6 billion to the shipbuilding account while trimming funding across several high-profile hull programs, USNI News reports. The reduction underscores growing congressional skepticism toward Navy acquisition schedules and cost overruns, coming a day after Senate Armed Services Committee Chairman Roger Wicker dismissed White House proposals to revert Ford-class aircraft carriers to steam catapults as a 'non-starter.'

Force-posture shifts also continued at sea: USNI News reports aircraft carrier USS George Washington (CVN-73) departed the Middle East after a three-month station and entered US 7th Fleet waters. Meanwhile, the Royal Navy carrier HMS Prince of Wales returned to Portsmouth after a six-month Atlantic and High North deployment, and The War Zone notes British Trident submarine HMS Vengeance completed a roughly 217-day submerged nuclear deterrence patrol.
sections.whyItMatters: A $20 billion Senate cut to Navy shipbuilding directly constrains the Pentagon's ability to expand fleet hull counts on schedule while carrier strike groups rotate rapidly between the Middle East and Indo-Pacific.

sections.heading: US Launches Unarmed ICBM Test Hours Before Trump Lands in China
sections.body:
The United States conducted an unarmed intercontinental ballistic missile test launch less than two hours before President Donald Trump landed in Shenzhen on Wednesday for the APEC summit and trilateral talks with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin, SCMP reports. The timing of the test added sharp strategic signaling to a summit where Washington is nominally seeking nuclear arms control discussions alongside trade talks.

In parallel, European defense planners are looking at long-range deterrence from orbit: The War Zone reports European states are exploring orbital deep-strike weapons concepts, though high launch and basing costs remain a major hurdle. Meanwhile, the US Air Force's Containerized Surface-to-Air Missile (Counter-Air Missile) program is taking shape around lower-cost modular interceptors, The War Zone adds.
sections.whyItMatters: Conducting an ICBM test hours before a Trump-Xi-Putin summit signals nuclear readiness even as leaders explore arms-control dialogue, while modular air defense and orbital strike concepts show allied militaries adapting for high-end deterrence.

sections.heading: Hegseth Unveils New US-Venezuela Military Deal on Caracas Visit
sections.body:
US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth unveiled a new bilateral military cooperation agreement with Venezuela during his first visit to Caracas since the US capture of Nicolas Maduro, Al Jazeera reports, restoring formal defense ties frozen since 2005. The pact marks a rapid geopolitical pivot in South America's northern tier, giving Washington renewed security access and training channels in a country long aligned with Moscow and Tehran.

Back in Washington, internal defense-industrial security and procurement oversight remained under pressure. The Hill reports federal prosecutors charged a Russian national with spying on employees at a major US defense technology firm over Ukraine's use of its systems, while Military Times notes a government watchdog flagged fraud and the Pentagon's ninth consecutive failed audit as top oversight priorities.
sections.whyItMatters: Re-establishing US-Venezuela military cooperation transforms Washington's security footprint in the Western Hemisphere, even as Russian espionage against defense-tech workers highlights persistent counterintelligence vulnerabilities.

sections.heading: Ukraine Strikes Kerch Bridge Again as Private Firms Run Air Defenses
sections.body:
Ukrainian forces struck the Kerch Bridge linking occupied Crimea to Russia for a third time in three days, The War Zone and Anadolu Agency report, prompting Moscow-appointed Crimean authorities to suspend bridge traffic for structural damage assessments. Ars Technica adds that Ukraine bypassed SpaceX's Starshield speed curbs over occupied territory by deploying homegrown relay drones to guide its long-range strike systems.

On the ground in Ukraine, Business Insider reports Kyiv's decision to let private defense manufacturers buy and operate their own air defense systems to protect factories has begun paying off against Russian strikes. Meanwhile, European and Pentagon officials clashed publicly over Ukraine support, the Wall Street Journal reports, as European allies convened in Berlin with US envoys.
sections.whyItMatters: Relay drones defeating satellite speed curbs and private factories operating dedicated air defenses show how Ukraine is improvising around external technical limits to keep pressure on Russian logistics.

sections.heading: Houthis Claim Riyadh Missile Strikes as CENTCOM Chief Visits Saudi Arabia
sections.body:
Regional air-defense tempo intensified across the Arabian Peninsula as Houthi forces claimed cruise missile attacks targeting Riyadh's international airport and financial center, the Times of Israel reports, while Anadolu Agency notes the Saudi-led coalition intercepted a Houthi ballistic missile and destroyed its launcher in Yemen's Saada province. Yemeni government forces also reported conducting over 700 operations that killed or wounded 142 Houthi commanders and fighters.

Amidst the widening Gulf exchanges—which The War Zone links to Iran's retaliation following US strikes on an Iranian island—Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman met the CENTCOM commander in Riyadh to coordinate military ties, Anadolu Agency reports. Separately, in Sudan, a Rapid Support Forces commander and troops defected to the Sudanese army as fighting continued in Darfur, Anadolu Agency notes.
sections.whyItMatters: Claimed cruise missile strikes toward Riyadh alongside Yemen ground operations indicate that Houthi long-range fire remains active despite coalition launcher strikes, keeping Gulf air defense readiness at peak strain.

bottomLine: US defense posture is being pulled in opposite directions: Senate appropriators are cutting $20 billion from Navy shipbuilding at home while the Pentagon tests ICBMs ahead of Shenzhen, signs a new military pact in Venezuela, and coordinates Gulf missile defenses with Riyadh. Meanwhile, Ukraine's relay-drone strikes on the Kerch Bridge demonstrate that tactical adaptation continues to outpace static export or satellite restrictions.
sources: USNI News, SCMP, The War Zone, Al Jazeera, The Hill, Military Times, Anadolu Agency, Business Insider, Ars Technica, Times of Israel, Wall Street Journal
